title: feat(types,plugin-kanban)!: retire ObjectKanbanSchema.onQuickAdd; the object-kanban path renders an internal board that takes the quick-add pair as props (objectui#11234)
body:
Fixes #11234
Clause-②: no (narrowing)

Retires `ObjectKanbanSchema.onQuickAdd` on `object-kanban` on both faces, completing ruling B of the director seat's decision batch #91 (`5583979207`, recorded on objectui#8285): the object-bound board does not grow an inline record-creation write path, and the Quick Add pair stays with a React host. Direction is option A of the PR objectui#11231 dev, as adopted in the card; no inline creation path is added, and `KanbanRenderer`'s host pair is unchanged.

## What changed

- **`@object-ui/types`**: `ObjectKanbanSchema.onQuickAdd` is `?: never` on the TypeScript face (`objectql.ts`), and `handlerKeyRefusal('onQuickAdd', 'retired', 'Quick Add handler')` on the zod mirror (`zod/objectql.zod.ts`). The JSON face still refuses the key by name with code `custom`; the guidance now says RETIRED instead of RUNTIME SLOT.
- **`@object-ui/plugin-kanban`**:
  - A new internal module `src/KanbanBoardCore.tsx` holds the board body that used to live in `KanbanRenderer`: the bucketing memo, the lazy `KanbanImpl`, and the Suspense fallback. It takes the Quick Add pair ONLY as explicit props (`quickAdd`, `onQuickAdd`), and its `schema` type is `KanbanRendererProps['schema']` with those two keys omitted, so a `schema.onQuickAdd` read written into it fails type-check. It is not re-exported from the `index.tsx` barrel.
  - `KanbanRenderer` (public) now renders `KanbanBoardCore` and passes `schema.quickAdd` / `schema.onQuickAdd`. Its props interface is byte-identical, and so is what a host gets.
  - `ObjectKanban` renders `KanbanBoardCore` and passes neither half. The old `quickAdd: undefined` line on `effectiveSchema` is removed, because nothing on this path reads `schema.quickAdd` any more; the comment in its place says where the cut now is.
  - Why the module move was needed: `check:handler-key-reads` refuses a `retired` disposition while a renderer reachable from the registration reads the key off the document. The `object-kanban` path reached `KanbanRenderer`'s `schema.onQuickAdd` read. After this change, the gate's census for `object-kanban` holds one row, `onCardClick [runtime-slot]`, read in `KanbanBoardCore.tsx`.
- **Docs**: `content/docs/plugins/plugin-kanban.mdx` (the handler-key paragraph and the "Quick Add is a React-host capability" section) and `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md` (the `ObjectKanbanSchema` handler-keys callout, and one clause of the `quickAdd` callout).
- **Changesets**: `.changeset/11234-object-kanban-onquickadd-retired.md`, with `minor` on `@object-ui/types` (a narrowing, breaking semantics stated in the body) and `patch` on `@object-ui/plugin-kanban` (no public props moved). Three pending entries that this release would otherwise ship with a false sentence are amended, one sentence each, with every other byte and the frontmatter unchanged: `8285-object-kanban-quick-add-retired.md` (its closing note said `onQuickAdd` stays a runtime slot), `7804-object-kanban-handler-keys-judged.md` (it said `onCardClick` and `onQuickAdd` are both runtime slots) and `8285-kanban-quickadd-html-diagnostic.md` (it said `onQuickAdd` is a runtime slot).

## Pins

- **JSON face, by name, and TS face `never`**: new `packages/types/src/__tests__/object-kanban-on-quick-add-retired-11234.test.ts`.
  - Runtime legs: the key is refused as `custom` at path `onQuickAdd`, for an action object and for a live function. The `.describe()` text is the parse message. A near-miss key is kept. The CLI union refuses a whole node carrying the key.
  - The retired-disposition leg reads RETIRED for `onQuickAdd` against `onCardClick` on the same arm and helper, which still reads RUNTIME SLOT. That `onCardClick` reading is the lit control.
  - Type-level pins: `Equal` to `undefined`, not `any`, not callable, and an `@ts-expect-error` on a literal that writes the key. The sibling slot `onCardClick` is still callable.
- **The host pair still draws and calls (control)**: `quickAddRetiredNotForwarded-8285.test.tsx` row 2, unchanged. `KanbanRenderer` with `quickAdd: true` plus a function draws one control per lane, and a submitted title reaches the host.
- **An `object-kanban` node draws no Quick Add**: the same file's row 1, unchanged, through the real registry and the real board. It was already green before this change, because `quickAdd` was cut. The readings that discriminate on `onQuickAdd` itself flip in two files, each with `onCardClick` as the lit control on the same render:
  - `handlerKeyDispositionsMeasured-7804.test.tsx` suite 2: the board receives `onQuickAdd: undefined` and `quickAdd: undefined`, while the authored `onCardClick` runs once.
  - `kanban-handler-slots-7664.test.tsx` suite 1.
- **Ablation** (below): re-declaring the key as a runtime slot turns the retired-disposition pin red on each face.

Ledger rows moved with it:
- the objectui#6124 ledger: the row moves from `RUNTIME_SLOT` to `RETIRED`, 61 + 21 becomes 60 + 22 with the total unchanged at 82, and the type blocks move the key from `KeepsFunction` to `RetiredIsNever`;
- `zod-mirror-parity`: `onQuickAdd` leaves the `objectql.zod.ts#ObjectKanbanSchema` drift entry, and the header key total goes 87 to 86 with its history sentence;
- the objectui#7340 docs census: 29 retired members, `objectql.ts` 2, and `onQuickAdd` joins the unambiguously retired names;
- the objectui#7804 and objectui#7664 plugin-kanban readings: suite 3 of 7664 now derives the read sites from both bodies, and adds a barrel pin that `KanbanBoardCore` is not published;
- `check-handler-key-read-sites.test.ts`: `onQuickAdd` leaves the `object-kanban` census, the arm reads `retired`, and the `onCardClick` row's file is `KanbanBoardCore.tsx`.

Three source-reading pins had to be re-pointed at the moved text:
- the objectui#9357 arity pin's `index.tsx` hop is now the hand-off to `KanbanBoardCore`;
- the objectui#8932 firing control finds the live board's lazy import in `KanbanBoardCore.tsx`;
- the objectui#8801 schema-channel end is now `KanbanBoardCore`'s signature.

## Measured producers of `onQuickAdd` on `object-kanban`: 0 in both repos

- **objectui** (this branch): tracked files naming `onQuickAdd`, excluding tests and markdown, number 7 at the final head. They are `KanbanImpl.tsx` (the board's props), `index.tsx` (the host face), the two declarations, one comment in the gate script, `KanbanBoardCore.tsx` (its internal prop pair), and one comment in `ObjectKanban.tsx`. None writes the key onto an `object-kanban` node. Lit control on the same instrument: 7 non-test files write a `type: 'object-kanban'` node, and 2 JSON files in `examples/schema-catalog` carry `object-kanban`. JSON/YAML files naming `onQuickAdd`: 0.
- **objectstack** `origin/main` `4d0b9cd54` (read-only `git grep`): `onQuickAdd` appears only in docs, CHANGELOGs, comments and diagnostic message text (`component.mdx`, the sdui-parser interim diagnostic and its test, the spec CHANGELOG, a `conversions/registry.ts` note). `packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts` has 0 hits for `onQuickAdd`. Lit control on the same instrument: `quickAdd` hits 17 files, `component.zod.ts` among them.

The file count, 16, is read from the JSON output. `eslint.config.js` configures no `projectService` and no `parserOptions.project`, so linting is not type-aware and this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file.

### Ablation: re-declare `onQuickAdd` as a runtime slot, one face at a time

Run on the committed head `e2bf34b97` through objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode, inside a script with its own `trap` restore, under the lock. The predictions were written before the run.

- **Zod leg**: `'retired'` becomes `'runtime-slot'` in `objectql.zod.ts`. The anchor went x1 to x0 and the blob `c106c73cb1ec` to `6b9fc742c9d5`. Vitest over the 11234 pin and the 6124 ledger read 2 failed, 341 passed. The two failures are exactly the predicted legs: the 11234 retired-disposition leg, and the 6124 "guidance wording distinguishes a runtime slot from a retired key" leg.
- **TS leg**: `onQuickAdd?: never;` becomes the callable in `objectql.ts`. The anchor went x1 to x0 and the blob `dde43cddfea1` to `afedc0cab24b`. `tsc -p packages/types/tsconfig.test.json` exited 2 with 5 errors:
  - the 11234 pin: TS2344 twice (tombstone, not-callable) and TS2578 (the `@ts-expect-error` became unused);
  - the 6124 `RetiredIsNever` row: TS2344;
  - `zod-mirror-parity`'s type-map ledger: TS2322, because the drift entry is owed again. This fifth error was not in the written prediction. It is the right direction, since the ledger answers to the faces.
- **Restore proven**: `git diff HEAD` over both paths is 0 bytes, both blob hashes equal HEAD's, and `git status --porcelain` has 0 lines.

## Acceptance notes (observations; nothing filed)

- Three pending changesets said `onQuickAdd` is, or stays, a runtime slot on `object-kanban`, which would ship false in the same release: `8285-object-kanban-quick-add-retired.md`, `7804-object-kanban-handler-keys-judged.md` and `8285-kanban-quickadd-html-diagnostic.md`. Each false sentence is amended in this PR, and the rest of each file, frontmatter included, is byte-identical. The seat added the three files to the claim's file surface.
- The objectui#6124 ledger's `RetiredIsNever` type block has no `ObjectKanbanSchema['onCardMove']` row. That key's `never` is pinned by a source read in the 7804 suite 3 leg instead. Not added here.
- A few comments still say "`KanbanRenderer`'s lazy boundary", and several tests' pre-warm comments say their `'../KanbanImpl'` specifier matches `index`'s. The lazy import now lives in `KanbanBoardCore.tsx`. It resolves to the same module, so the pre-warm imports still hit the cache. The comments are not swept; per AGENTS.md they get repaired when a change touches those files anyway. I fixed the ones on lines this change touched.
- The retired guidance text is the shared `handlerKeyRefusal` wording (the node-type remedy). The practical remedy for this key, mounting `KanbanRenderer`, is carried by the TS docblock, the docs and the changeset, the same as for `onCardMove`.
- The card body says `Clause-②: yes`; the PM claim says `no (narrowing)`. This body copies the claim's line, as the dispatch order directs.
